---
title: "hb_area() Engines: INLA vs JAX (CPU, Apple GPU, CUDA) vs tipsae"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6, dpi = 110)
library(ggplot2)

bench_dir <- Filter(dir.exists, c(file.path("..", "..", "inst", "extdata"),
                                  file.path("inst", "extdata")))[1]
bench_files <- list.files(bench_dir, pattern = "^hb_engine_benchmark.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
bench <- lapply(bench_files, readRDS)
tm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(bench, `[[`, "timings"))
ag <- do.call(rbind, lapply(bench, `[[`, "agreement"))
metas <- lapply(bench, `[[`, "meta")

machines <- unique(tm$machine)
cloud <- grepl("Colab|Kaggle", machines)
machines <- c(machines[!cloud], machines[cloud])
has_cuda <- "cuda" %in% tm$engine

engine_labels <- c(inla = "INLA (inla_engine)",
                   cpu = "JAX NUTS, CPU",
                   metal = "JAX NUTS, Apple GPU (Metal)",
                   cuda = "JAX NUTS, NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)",
                   tipsae = "tipsae (Stan NUTS)")
engine_colours <- c(inla = "#1D6A5C", cpu = "#E69F00", metal = "#7B5EA7",
                    cuda = "#76B900", tipsae = "#C0392B")
design_labels <- c(gaussian = "Spatial Fay-Herriot (Gaussian)", beta = "Spatial Beta (proportions)")
short_labels <- c(gaussian = "Gaussian", beta = "Beta")

used <- intersect(names(engine_labels), unique(tm$engine))
tm$engine_f <- factor(tm$engine, levels = used)
tm$design_f <- factor(design_labels[tm$design], levels = design_labels)
tm$machine_f <- factor(tm$machine, levels = machines)

fmt_s <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "-", ifelse(x < 10, sprintf("%.1f s", x), sprintf("%s s", format(round(x), big.mark = ","))))
}
fmt_n <- function(n) format(n, big.mark = ",")
time_of <- function(machine, design, engine, n, col = "time_warm") {
  v <- tm[tm$machine == machine & tm$design == design & tm$engine == engine & tm$n == n, col]
  if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else v[1]
}
gpu_of <- function(machine) {
  e <- intersect(c("metal", "cuda"), tm$engine[tm$machine == machine])
  if (length(e) == 0) NA_character_ else e[1]
}
```

`hb_area()` can be estimated by two engines:

- **`inla_engine()`** (default): integrated nested Laplace approximation with
  [INLA](https://www.r-inla.org).
- **`jax_engine()`**: full MCMC with NumPyro's No-U-Turn sampler on
  [JAX](https://jax.readthedocs.io). It runs on the CPU, on an NVIDIA GPU
  (`device = "cuda"`) or on the GPU of Apple silicon (`device = "metal"`).

This page compares the speed of both engines, on the CPU and on a GPU, and
how closely their estimates agree. The comparison uses spatial area-level
models. For the Beta model it also includes the
[tipsae](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tipsae) package, which fits the
same model by MCMC in Stan.

```{r pending, results = "asis"}
if (!has_cuda) {
  cat("> **NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) results pending.** They will be added here. They can be reproduced",
      "with the notebooks linked at the end of this page.\n")
}
```

## Setup

**Models.**

- **Data:** a regular grid of $D$ cells with queen adjacency, simulated by
  `sim_area_data(D = n, W = W, n_unsampled = 0, seed = 42 + n)`.
- **Gaussian:** `hb_area(y_gaussian ~ x1 + x2, spatial = "besag")`, a
  Fay-Herriot model with an intrinsic CAR (Besag) area effect.
- **Beta:** `hb_area(y_beta ~ x1 + x2, family = "beta", spatial = "besag")`.
  tipsae fits it with `fit_sae(likelihood = "beta", spatial_error = TRUE)`,
  which also uses an ICAR effect.

tipsae is run up to $D = `r fmt_n(max(tm$n[tm$engine == "tipsae"]))`$ only;
larger grids take too long and need too much memory.

```{r setup-table}
py_txt <- function(py) {
  if (is.null(py)) return("-")
  py <- py[!is.na(py)]
  paste(sprintf("%s %s", names(py), py), collapse = ", ")
}
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(metas, function(m) data.frame(
  Machine = m$machine,
  CPU = sprintf("%s (%d cores, %.0f GB RAM)", m$cpu, m$cpu_cores, m$ram_gb),
  GPU = ifelse(is.na(m$gpu), "-", m$gpu),
  Software = sprintf("R %s; fastsae %s; INLA %s; tipsae %s; %s",
                     sub("R version ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", m$r_version), m$fastsae, m$inla,
                     ifelse(is.na(m$tipsae), "-", m$tipsae), py_txt(m$python)),
  Date = m$date
))))
```

Each engine runs in a separate R process, because JAX fixes its device at
the first fit of a session. Every fit is run `r metas[[1]]$reps` times on the
same data. The first run includes JAX compilation; the tables and figure show
the faster, warm run. JAX uses the `jax_engine()` defaults (2 chains × 1,000
draws after 500 warmup), and tipsae uses its own defaults. The code is in
[`benchmarks/bench_hb_area_engines.R`](https://github.com/ridsonap/fastsae/blob/main/benchmarks/bench_hb_area_engines.R).

**Comparing machines.** Times measured on different machines are not
comparable with each other. The ratios within one machine are: GPU vs CPU,
and INLA vs tipsae.

## Computation time

```{r time-plot, fig.height = 2.3 + 2.3 * length(machines), fig.cap = "Warm computation time (log scales). Lower is faster. One row per machine."}
ggplot(tm, aes(n, time_warm, colour = engine_f)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(machine_f ~ design_f, labeller = labeller(machine_f = label_wrap_gen(14))) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = function(x) paste(format(x, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE), "s")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = engine_colours[used], labels = engine_labels[used], name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Number of domains (D)", y = "Time (seconds)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

```{r time-table}
keys <- unique(tm[, c("machine", "design", "n")])
keys <- keys[order(match(keys$machine, machines), match(keys$design, names(design_labels)), keys$n), ]
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
  k <- keys[i, ]
  gpu <- gpu_of(k$machine)
  t_inla <- time_of(k$machine, k$design, "inla", k$n)
  t_cpu <- time_of(k$machine, k$design, "cpu", k$n)
  t_gpu <- if (is.na(gpu)) NA_real_ else time_of(k$machine, k$design, gpu, k$n)
  t_tip <- time_of(k$machine, k$design, "tipsae", k$n)
  data.frame(
    Machine = k$machine,
    Model = short_labels[[k$design]],
    D = fmt_n(k$n),
    INLA = fmt_s(t_inla),
    `JAX CPU` = fmt_s(t_cpu),
    `JAX GPU` = if (is.na(gpu)) "-" else paste0(fmt_s(t_gpu), " (", gpu, ")"),
    `GPU vs CPU` = ifelse(is.na(t_gpu) | is.na(t_cpu), "-",
                          ifelse(t_gpu > t_cpu, sprintf("%.1fx slower", t_gpu / t_cpu),
                                 sprintf("**%.1fx faster**", t_cpu / t_gpu))),
    tipsae = fmt_s(t_tip),
    `INLA vs tipsae` = ifelse(is.na(t_tip), "-", sprintf("%sx faster", fmt_n(round(t_tip / t_inla)))),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lllrrrrrr")
```

```{r findings}
crossover <- function(machine, design) {
  gpu <- gpu_of(machine)
  if (is.na(gpu)) return(NA_character_)
  ns <- sort(unique(tm$n[tm$machine == machine & tm$design == design & tm$engine == gpu]))
  wins <- ns[vapply(ns, function(n) {
    isTRUE(time_of(machine, design, gpu, n) < time_of(machine, design, "cpu", n))
  }, logical(1))]
  if (length(wins) == 0) {
    sprintf("the CPU is faster at every size tested for the %s model", short_labels[[design]])
  } else {
    sprintf("the GPU is faster from $D = %s$ for the %s model", fmt_n(min(wins)), short_labels[[design]])
  }
}
gpu_txt <- vapply(machines, function(m) {
  gpu <- gpu_of(m)
  if (is.na(gpu)) return(NA_character_)
  sprintf("On %s (%s): %s.", m, c(metal = "Metal", cuda = "CUDA")[[gpu]],
          paste(vapply(names(design_labels), function(d) crossover(m, d), character(1)),
                collapse = ", and "))
}, character(1))
gpu_txt <- paste(gpu_txt[!is.na(gpu_txt)], collapse = " ")

tip <- tm[tm$engine == "tipsae", ]
tip_txt <- if (nrow(tip) == 0) "" else {
  m <- machines[machines %in% tip$machine][1]
  n_tip <- max(tip$n[tip$machine == m])
  both <- tip[tip$machine == m, "n"]
  r <- vapply(both, function(n) time_of(m, "beta", "tipsae", n) / time_of(m, "beta", "cpu", n), numeric(1))
  s <- sprintf(paste0("At $D = %s$ on %s, tipsae takes %s for the spatial Beta model, ",
                 "INLA takes %s (%sx faster), and JAX on the CPU takes %s."),
          fmt_n(n_tip), m, fmt_s(time_of(m, "beta", "tipsae", n_tip)),
          fmt_s(time_of(m, "beta", "inla", n_tip)),
          fmt_n(round(time_of(m, "beta", "tipsae", n_tip) / time_of(m, "beta", "inla", n_tip))),
          fmt_s(time_of(m, "beta", "cpu", n_tip)))
  sprintf("%s So the JAX engine on the CPU is %.0fx to %.0fx faster than tipsae on the sizes both ran.",
          s, min(r), max(r))
}
m1 <- machines[1]
n_max <- max(tm$n[tm$machine == m1])
```

The results:

- **INLA is the fastest engine at every size.** It does not sample. For
  example, on `r m1` the spatial Gaussian model at
  $D = `r fmt_n(n_max)`$ takes `r fmt_s(time_of(m1, "gaussian", "inla", n_max))`.
- **tipsae.** `r tip_txt`
- **The JAX engine's time grows quickly with $D$ for spatial models.** It
  represents the ICAR effect through the eigenvectors of the $D \times D$
  graph Laplacian. Computing them costs $O(D^3)$ once, and each gradient
  evaluation then costs $O(D^2)$. Dense matrix work of this kind is where a
  GPU helps.
- **CPU or GPU?** `r gpu_txt` The GPU has a fixed cost per fit (on Metal,
  every pass through NUTS' tree-building loop waits for the GPU and the CPU to
  synchronise), so it pays off only once $D$ is large.
  `jax_engine(device = "auto")` uses CUDA when an NVIDIA GPU is present and
  the CPU otherwise, including on macOS.

## Agreement of the estimates

Every engine is compared with INLA on the same machine and data. `cor` is
the correlation of the posterior means, `max |diff|` is the largest absolute
difference between them, and `sd ratio` is the median ratio of the
posterior standard deviations (engine / INLA).

```{r agreement}
ag <- ag[order(match(ag$machine, machines), match(ag$design, names(design_labels)),
               match(ag$engine, names(engine_labels)), ag$n), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Machine = ag$machine,
  Model = short_labels[ag$design],
  Engine = c(cpu = "JAX CPU", metal = "JAX Metal", cuda = "JAX CUDA", tipsae = "tipsae")[ag$engine],
  D = fmt_n(ag$n),
  cor = sprintf("%.4f", ag$cor_hb),
  `max |diff|` = signif(ag$max_abs_diff_hb, 2),
  `sd ratio` = sprintf("%.3f", ag$median_ratio_sd),
  check.names = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r agreement-text}
jx <- ag[ag$engine %in% c("cpu", "metal", "cuda"), ]
tp <- ag[ag$engine == "tipsae", ]
rh <- tm[tm$engine != "inla", ]
```

- **JAX engines.** On every device, the posterior means agree with INLA with
  correlations of at least `r sprintf("%.4f", floor(min(jx$cor_hb) * 1e4) / 1e4)`,
  and the same holds across devices. The GPU evaluates floating-point
  operations in a different order from the CPU, so the chains differ
  slightly, but they give the same estimates.
- **tipsae.** `r if (nrow(tp) > 0) sprintf("tipsae agrees with INLA with correlations of at least %.3f. Its posterior standard deviations are %s (median ratio %.2f to %.2f), probably because the two packages use different priors.", floor(min(tp$cor_hb) * 1e3) / 1e3, ifelse(max(tp$median_ratio_sd) < 1, "smaller", "different"), min(tp$median_ratio_sd), max(tp$median_ratio_sd)) else ""`
- **Convergence.** Over all JAX fits, the largest split R-hat is
  `r sprintf("%.3f", max(rh$rhat_max[rh$engine != "tipsae"], na.rm = TRUE))`.
  `r if (any(rh$engine == "tipsae")) { tr <- rh[rh$engine == "tipsae", ]; worst <- tr[which.max(tr$rhat_max), ]; sprintf("For tipsae it is %.3f (at $D = %s$ on %s)%s.", worst$rhat_max, fmt_n(worst$n), worst$machine, if (worst$rhat_max > 1.05) ", above the usual 1.05 threshold, so its default run length is not quite enough there" else "") } else ""`

## Using a GPU

```r
# One-time setup of the Python environment (CUDA on Linux/Windows, Metal on Apple silicon)
fastsae::setup_numpyro_env(device = "cuda")   # or device = "metal"

# In a new R session: request the GPU before any other JAX fit
fit <- hb_area(y ~ x1 + x2, vardir = "vardir", data = df, spatial = "besag", W = W,
               engine = jax_engine(device = "cuda"))
fit$device
```

**Metal.** jax-metal does not implement two operations used by NumPyro's NUTS
sampler: the bit count `popcnt`, and some `lax.cond` statements with constant
outputs. With `device = "metal"`, fastsae replaces both with equivalent
operations and samples the chains sequentially. If a model still cannot be
compiled on Metal, the fit falls back to the CPU with a warning.

**Reproduce the CUDA results.** Two notebooks install fastsae, INLA, tipsae
and JAX with CUDA, then run the same benchmark:

- **Kaggle** (recommended):
  [`benchmarks/kaggle/hb_area_engines_kaggle.ipynb`](https://github.com/ridsonap/fastsae/blob/main/benchmarks/kaggle/hb_area_engines_kaggle.ipynb).
  Import it into a Kaggle notebook. It is a Python notebook, because Kaggle
  gives GPUs to Python notebooks, and it installs R itself. Choose a GPU
  accelerator and turn the internet on. Then use *Save & Run All*, which
  runs the whole benchmark on Kaggle's servers without the browser open.
- **Google Colab**:
  [`benchmarks/colab/hb_area_engines_colab.ipynb`](https://colab.research.google.com/github/ridsonap/fastsae/blob/main/benchmarks/colab/hb_area_engines_colab.ipynb).
  Choose an R runtime with a T4 GPU and run all cells. Keep the tab open
  until the run finishes.

**In short:**

- For most surveys (hundreds to a few thousand domains), `inla_engine()` is
  the fastest choice.
- For full MCMC, the JAX engine is much faster than Stan via tipsae, on
  the CPU alone.
- A GPU becomes worthwhile for the JAX engine on large spatial models.
